headline: Stocks tumble, investors lose Rs474bn as US strikes Iran, ceasefire 'effectively over'
summary: Wednesday session: KSE-100 fell 4,626.18 points (-2.48%) to 181,629.37, Rs474bn wiped off market cap; ten heavyweights (UBL, FFC, ENGROH, LUCK, HUBC, HBL, PPL, OGDC, MARI, MCB) cut ~2,331 points; volume surged 57.49% to 1.54bn shares on US air strikes on Iran and rising crude.

headline: PSX Closing Bell: Red Closes the Curtain
summary: Thursday: KSE-100 -369.69 points (-0.20%) to 181,259.67 amid lingering US-Iran tension; gainers GHNI +10.00%, GAL +5.99%, HCAR +3.88%; losers AKBL -3.43%, MEBL -2.24%, MCB -2.11%.

headline: PSX settles higher as KSE-100 adds nearly 1,000 points
summary: Friday: KSE-100 +982.10 points (+0.54%) to 182,241.78 on value-buying; volume 948.776m shares worth Rs38.413bn; market cap up to Rs20.503trn; 292 advancers vs 169 decliners.

headline: Weekly Market Roundup: KSE-100 down 1.69% WoW on Middle East tensions
summary: Week ended Jul 10: KSE-100 -3,130.43 points (-1.69%) WoW to 182,241.78 from 185,372.21; E&P worst sector (-648.16 index points), Fertilizer -447.95, Cement -436.01, Banks -344.47, Refinery sole gainer +115.39; foreigners net buyers Rs2.37bn ($8.53m).

headline: Petrol, diesel prices hiked by Rs13.18 and Rs13.80 per litre
summary: Government raised ex-depot prices effective Jul 11, 2026: petrol +Rs13.18 to Rs310.71/litre (from Rs297.53), HSD +Rs13.80 to Rs323.30/litre (from Rs309.50) - inflationary shock, direct read-through for OMCs and refiners.

headline: SBP FX reserves jump $1.94bn to $18.47bn
summary: SBP-held reserves rose $1.94bn (+11.76% WoW) to $18.47bn in the week ended Jul 3, 2026 - supportive for PKR and macro stability.

headline: Worker remittances fall to $3.47bn in June
summary: June 2026 remittances $3.47bn, down 18.3% MoM but up 2% YoY.

headline: Bank Alfalah's Rs20bn Tier-2 TFC fully subscribed
summary: BAFL's Rs20,000,000,000 Tier-2 Term Finance Certificate issue fully subscribed with SBP approval - strengthens capital base.

headline: OGDC's entire BESOS trust shareholding transferred back to GoP
summary: Transfer of OGDC shares held under the BESOS employee trust back to the Government of Pakistan completed - routine shareholding change.

headline: PSX reconstitutes JS Momentum Factor Index
summary: Effective Jul 7, 2026: added SSGC, SNGP, GAL, PSX, ILP, THCCL, PIAHCLA, TOMCL; removed AIRLINK, FCCL, FrieslandCampina, FFC, PPL, PTC, SAZEW, TRG; MLCF and DGKC now top weights at 20% each.

headline: ADB slashes Pakistan FY27 growth forecast
summary: ADB cut its Pakistan FY27 growth forecast; economy expanded 3.7% in FY2025-26 per the briefing.

headline: Record 48% surge in stock market investors in FY26
summary: SECP data: 190,277 new investors joined PSX in FY2025-26, a 48% surge - structural positive for exchange volumes.

headline: RDA attracts $306m in June
summary: Roshan Digital Account inflows of $306m in June 2026; cumulative total $13,365m.

headline: PKR holds firm below 278.20
summary: Rupee settled at Rs278.05 per USD, a modest gain, despite oil-driven import cost concerns.

headline: Pakistan's IT sector exports $4.5bn in FY26 amid Asia-Pacific push
summary: IT exports reached approximately $4.5bn in FY2025-26 - supportive backdrop for listed tech exporters.

headline: SECP unveils digital KYC for investors
summary: SECP introduced a digital KYC framework to simplify access to capital markets and insurance - onboarding tailwind for retail participation.

headline: Govt showcases record Sukuk issuance, debt market growth
summary: PSX and Ministry of Finance held an investor briefing on debt management strategy, record Sukuk issuance and fiscal reforms.

headline: Meezan Bank, Iqra University introduce Islamic FinTech centre
summary: MEBL partnered with Iqra University to establish the IU Centre for Excellence in Islamic FinTech - reputational, not financial.

headline: PSX opens week in the red, plummets amid US-Iran Strait of Hormuz escalation
summary: Monday session (intraday): KSE-100 Index lost 2,215.27 points at 10:19am to stand at 180,026.5 (previous close 182,241.77); as of 12:33pm down 1,706.67 points (-0.94%) to 180,535.10; Business Recorder later reported the index shed 2,202.63 points to 180,039.14. Driver: US and Iran exchanged fresh strikes over the Strait of Hormuz, Iran claimed to have closed the strait, oil prices jumped over 4%; across-the-board selling in autos, cement, banks, E&P, OMCs and power, with HUBCO, MARI, OGDC, PSO, SSGC, SNGPL, MCB, MEBL, NBP and UBL trading in the red; refinery sector was the lone positive per Dawn.

headline: Govt unveils new plan to fast track $6 billion refinery upgrade projects
summary: Petroleum Division submitted amendments to the Brownfield Refining Policy 2023 to the Cabinet Committee on Energy: refineries (PARCO, Attock Refinery/ARL, Pakistan Refinery/PRL, National Refinery/NRL, Cnergyico) that sign OGRA Upgrade Agreements within 90 days get a seven-year package - minimum 10% customs/regulatory duty maintained on imported gasoline and diesel for seven years, a 10% deemed duty incentive on locally produced gasoline/diesel, and sales tax exemption on imported plant, machinery, equipment and materials - to unlock nearly $6 billion in upgrades.

headline: PSX Closing Bell: Falls Off A Cliff
summary: Monday final close: KSE-100 ended at 179,927.04, down 2,314.73 points (-1.27%) from previous close of 182,241.77; KSE-100 volume 365.01m shares, All-Share Index volume 845.28m shares, market value traded Rs35.55bn; breadth 13 advancers vs 87 decliners of 100 index companies; top gainers GHNI +5.60%, CNERGY +3.72%, GHGL +1.97%, ATRL +1.93%, RMPL +0.69%; top losers TGL -4.03%, HGFA -3.38%, DGKC -3.20%, MLCF -3.17%, POWER -2.99%; report attributes the drop to the surge in international oil prices and heightened geopolitical uncertainty (US-Iran Strait of Hormuz), prompting broad-based selling in banking, cement, fertilizer and energy stocks.

headline: PKR strengthens again, hits 195-day winning run vs USD
summary: Rupee added 3.08 paisa in Monday's interbank session to settle at Rs278.02/USD (from Friday's close of Rs278.05), extending a 195-consecutive-day winning streak vs the dollar (cumulative +Rs3.4018, +1.22% over the streak); intraday band Rs278.20-278.00; open market Rs278.80 buy / Rs279.10 sell.

headline: Pakistan car sales jump 39% in FY26
summary: FY26 cumulative car/LCV/van/jeep sales reached 206,436 units, +39.4% YoY vs FY25's 148,042; June 2026 sales 22,741 units (+4.4% YoY, +28.8% MoM), though passenger cars alone fell 12.9% YoY in June (15,378 units) while LCVs/vans/jeeps rose 79.0% YoY (7,363 units); June brand figures cited: Suzuki 7,719 units (Alto 7,239, Every 480, Cultus 439, Swift 1,668), Toyota 2,650 units, Honda 2,594 units, Hyundai 288 units - no PSX-ticker-level breakdown given in the article.

headline: Sazgar produces 2,488 three-wheelers, 2,374 four-wheelers in June 2026
summary: SAZEW June 2026 output: 2,488 three-wheelers produced (3,267 sold) and 2,374 four-wheelers produced (2,720 sold), combined 4,862 units produced vs 5,987 sold; vs May 2026, four-wheeler production +47.5% (sales +69.6%) and three-wheeler production +52.5% (sales +99.7%) - sales outpacing production indicates inventory drawdown.

headline: Nestle Pakistan board meeting notice posted
summary: PSX corporate announcements / DPS company page for NESTLE show a board meeting notice posted Jul 13, 2026; agenda/date of the meeting itself not specified in the source pages reviewed - routine notice, no dividend or results figure disclosed yet.

headline: PSX plunges over 2% intraday as US reimposes naval blockade on Iran
summary: Tuesday intraday, from previous close of 179,927.04/179,927.05 (Monday): Dawn reported KSE-100 at 176,462.15, down 3,464.89 points (-1.93%); Pakistan Observer reported it down 3,733.34 points to 176,193.70 (-2.07%); Business Recorder reported it shedding over 3,600 points in opening minutes to 176,309.50 as of 9:43am, down 3,617.54 points (-2.01%), with index-heavy MARI, OGDC, PPL, HUBCO, MCB, MEBL and UBL trading in the red across autos, cement, banks, E&P, OMCs and power sectors. Driver: President Trump announced the US is reinstating a naval blockade of Iranian shipping through the Strait of Hormuz effective Jul 14 (CENTCOM cited 4:00pm ET start), plus a 20% fee on cargo transiting the strait; Brent crude +$1.50 to $84.80/bbl (+1.8%), WTI +$1.70 to $79.84/bbl (+2.2%), four-week highs; AKD Securities' Awais Ashraf quoted: 'The decline is broad-based, with cyclical sectors witnessing the sharpest percentage losses amid heightened uncertainty.'

source: Business Recorder / Geo News / Dawn / Express Tribune
headline: Selling grips PSX, KSE-100 tumbles nearly 5,000 points as US reimposes naval blockade on Iran (session deepens)
summary: Same Tuesday Strait-of-Hormuz story continued to deepen through the session (previous close 179,927.04): Business Recorder reported the index at 174,942.03 as of 12:04pm, down 4,985.01 points (-2.77%); Geo News reported an intraday low of 174,615.03, down 5,312.01 points (-2.95%), with an intraday high of 178,112.04 (-1,815 points, -1.01%); Dawn/Express Tribune reported 175,338.25 (-4,588.79 pts) at 12:30pm and 175,683.38 (-4,243.66 pts, -2.36%) at 12:44pm; across-the-board selling continued in autos, cement, banks, E&P, OMCs and power, with MARI, OGDC, PPL, HUBCO, MCB, MEBL and UBL still trading in the red; no confirmed final closing-bell figure found in the sources reviewed as of this cycle.

headline: National Foods - Material Information: Establishment of National Foods Gulf FZE
summary: NATF's DPS company announcements page shows a material information filing dated Jul 14, 2026 titled 'Establishment of National Foods Gulf FZE'; no investment amount, ownership structure or business purpose figures disclosed in the source page reviewed - overseas subsidiary expansion, follow-up to prior National Foods Gulf-entity activity.

headline: PSX Strait-of-Hormuz sell-off deepens further intraday - KSE-100 last quoted down over 6,000 points
summary: Continuation of the same Tuesday Strait-of-Hormuz story (previous close 179,927.05): Investing.com's Karachi 100 quote page, timestamped 06:05:45 and marked 'Delayed Data', showed the index last at 173,840.94, down 6,086.12 points (-3.38%), with the day's low at 173,785.30 and day's open at 178,053.66 - a deeper decline than the 174,615.03 low and 175,683.38 (-2.36%) level reported by Business Recorder/Geo News/Dawn/Express Tribune earlier in the same session (logged in the prior newslog entry). No PSX/DPS-sourced or Mettis Global 'Closing Bell' final print was found in sources reviewed this cycle to confirm this as the official close; flagged as the latest available read on the ongoing sell-off pending confirmation.

headline: Select Technologies raises Rs3.02bn through IPO, becomes 1st PSX listing of new fiscal year
summary: Select Technologies Limited, a Pakistani smartphone and consumer-appliances maker, raised Rs3.02bn via IPO of 88.9m ordinary shares (10% of post-issue paid-up capital); floor price Rs28.00/share, strike price discovered at Rs34.00/share (21% premium over floor) after book-building; issue oversubscribed 3.23x with ~13,000 investors participating (banks, mutual funds, insurers, pension funds, brokerages, HNWIs, retail). Not currently a KSE100/KMI30 universe constituent - logged for macro/primary-market sentiment context only; ticker symbol not confirmed in source reviewed.

headline: Dada Partners advises Nishat Group on Pakistan's largest private cross-border listed-company acquisition (Rafhan Maize)
summary: Nishat Group acquired 73.9% of Rafhan Maize Products Company Limited (RMPL) for approximately PKR 66 billion - 51% bought from majority shareholder Ingredion Incorporated (USA, which retains a strategic minority stake), 20.5% from a minority shareholder, and 2.4% via mandatory public offer - taking Nishat Group's total stake to a super-majority 75.9%; described in the article as the largest private-sector cross-border M&A of a listed Pakistani company, excluding privatizations. Dada Partners (Private) Limited was exclusive financial advisor to Nishat Group; Cornelius, Lane and Mufti (CLM) was legal counsel; Next Capital was Manager to the Offer.

headline: Hormuz tensions wipe out over 6,400 points at PSX - KSE-100 confirmed close
summary: Tuesday final close confirmed: Express Tribune reported KSE-100 'closed at 173,518.82, down 6,408.23 points, or 3.56%, from the previous close of 179,927.05, as selling intensified throughout the session'; volume 912.6m shares, value Rs45.6bn traded, 498 companies traded (40 up, 439 down, 19 unchanged); major decliners named: UBL, Engro Holdings, Fauji Fertiliser, Lucky Cement, Meezan Bank, OGDC, HBL, PPL and MCB Bank. Corroborating Dawn report (timestamped 3:00pm PKT) had the index at 173,839.01, down 6,088.03 points (-3.38%), quoting AKD Securities director of research Awais Ashraf: 'The decline is broad-based, with cyclical sectors witnessing the sharpest percentage losses amid heightened uncertainty over the medium-term outlook due to the emerging geopolitical situation.' Same Strait-of-Hormuz naval-blockade driver as prior entries this cycle; this is the deepest and now-final read of Tuesday's session, superseding the earlier intraday/delayed-quote entries logged above.

headline: Pakistan retires record Rs4.7tr debt ahead of maturity
summary: Pakistan retired Rs4.7 trillion (approx. $17bn) of public debt ahead of maturity - described as the largest early-retirement liability-management exercise in the country's history; composition 51% owed to SBP, 49% market debt/government securities; Adviser to the Finance Minister Khurram Schehzad called it the 'largest and most sustained liability management operation,' with average maturity of public debt extended from 2.7 years (FY24) to 3.8 years (FY26) - supportive for macro stability and refinancing risk, no direct PSX-ticker impact disclosed.

headline: PSX Opening Bell: Bulls Set the Early Pace
summary: Wednesday early trade (published 09:50am PKT), rebounding off Tuesday's 173,518.81 close: KSE-100 at 176,202.88, up 2,684.07 points (+1.55%), intraday high 176,344.73 (+2,825.92 pts); driver: 'investors engaged in value buying after heavy selloffs' in the prior session; breadth 89 advancers vs 6 decliners, 1 unchanged, 4 untraded of the 100 index companies, volume 21.22m shares; top % gainers YOUW +4.44%, SCBPL +3.82%, FATIMA +3.60%, KTML +3.37%, CHCC +3.31%; largest point contributors UBL +373.08, MEBL +170.87, ENGROH +156.53, FFC +148.66, HUBC +124.02.

headline: PSX Closing Bell: Every Rose Has Its Thorn
summary: Tuesday confirmed close detail (same Strait-of-Hormuz selloff already logged above at impact 5; this is Mettis's own closing-bell print, published Jul 14, 2026 4:03pm PKT, with sector breakdown not previously captured): KSE-100 closed at 173,518.81, down 6,408.23 points (-3.56%); volume 409.23m shares, value traded Rs45.61bn, 620,763 trades across 498 companies; breadth 40 higher, 439 lower, 19 unchanged; top losers GHNI -8.74%, TRG -8.21%, GAL -8.01%, AKBL -7.65%, MLCF -7.55%; sole listed top gainer UPFL +0.36%. Reason given: 'escalating geopolitical tensions and a surge in global oil prices' after Trump's 20% Hormuz-transit fee and Iranian port blockade announcement, triggering 'widespread risk-off sentiment.'

headline: Bulls snap losing streak as PSX gains 1,000 points during intraday trade
summary: Wednesday confirmed final close (published 05:05pm PKT): KSE-100 settled at 175,285.78, up 1,766.97 points (+1.02%) from Tuesday's close of 173,518.81; intraday high 176,701.38 at 10:02am, superseding the morning's 'Opening Bell' read logged earlier this cycle. Drivers cited: value buying after the prior session's steep declines (Mettis Global); Trump replacing the proposed 20% Strait of Hormuz transit toll with GCC investment commitments, per AKD Securities research director Awais Ashraf; softer-than-expected US inflation data easing concerns over further Fed rate hikes, supporting capital-flow outlook and the rupee; Brent crude +1.2% to $85.72/bbl and WTI +0.8% to $79.98/bbl on the continuing US naval blockade of Iranian ports and regional tensions. No specific tickers/sectors named in the source reviewed.

headline: PSX continues recovery as KSE-100 index gains 2,600 points in early trade
summary: Thursday morning (published/updated 11:11am PKT): KSE-100 at 177,890.27, up 2,604.49 points (+1.49%) from Wednesday's close of 175,285.78; Dawn attributes the continued rebound to 'value-hunting by equity investors' following Tuesday's panic-driven Strait-of-Hormuz selloff and Wednesday's partial recovery; no specific sectors or analysts named in the source reviewed.

headline: Textile exports stagnate at $17.9bn in FY26; June exports drop 16.71% YoY
summary: FY26 textile exports totalled $17.93bn, up just 0.26% YoY from $17.88bn in FY25 (Dawn) - 'one of the weakest performances in recent years' - missing the annual export target by $4.87bn, partly attributed to the suspension of trade with Afghanistan (an export market worth nearly $1.5bn); by product, readymade garments +3.87% in value, yarn +12.40%, knitwear -0.88%, cotton cloth -7.55%. Mettis Global's own figures: June 2026 textile exports were $1.27bn, down 16.71% YoY and 22.72% MoM (from $1.64bn in May), with knitwear -19.99%, readymade garments -12.43%, bed wear -23.29%; textile group products were 53.52% of total June exports. No individual company figures disclosed in either source.

headline: Large-Scale Manufacturing grows 5.77pc despite May slump
summary: LSM sector posted 5.77% YoY growth in the first 11 months (Jul-May) of FY26; QIM index 121.65 vs 115.02 in the corresponding prior-year period, though May alone contracted 0.98% YoY (+1.21% MoM vs April). Top contributors to growth: automobiles +1.53pp (production +58.82%), food products +1.36pp (output +7.75%), garments +1.20pp (exports +7.31%), petroleum products +0.78pp (coke and petroleum +10.56%). Detractors: pharmaceuticals -8.07%, iron & steel -7.49%, chemicals -2.64%, fertilizers -2.25%, textiles -0.09% - sector-level aggregate data only, no individual companies named in the source reviewed.

headline: PSX sets Rs925bn target for Jul-Sep 2026
summary: Published 10:14am PKT: PSX issued a revised Jul-Sep 2026 government-securities auction calendar, on the advice of the Debt Management Office (DMO) of the Ministry of Finance, targeting cumulative Rs925bn issuance of Government of Pakistan Hybrid Sukuk (GHS) and Ijarah Sukuk (GIS) - Rs625bn via Variable Rental Rate instruments across five auctions and Rs300bn via Fixed Rental Rate/Fixed Rate Zero Coupon structures across two auctions, tenors from 3-month to 10-year. This is a routine government debt-auction calendar administered via PSX, not a PSX-company revenue or earnings figure.

headline: Pakistan's FY26 import bill climbs 8.15%
summary: Published 10:11am PKT: FY26 import bill totalled $69.76bn (Rs19.59trn), up 8.15% YoY in dollar terms (8.72% in rupee terms) from $64.51bn (Rs18.02trn) in FY25. Breakdown by commodity group: petroleum $16.86bn (+5.76% YoY, largest contributor), food $9.15bn (+11.66%), metal $6.31bn (+12.07%), transport $4.06bn (+66.36%, sharpest growth); textile was the only major category to decline, at $6.46bn (-12.16% YoY).
